summary: Treat highWaterMark as a backpressure threshold measured in bytes/code-units/objects, not a hard memory cap.

target.notes: Runtime must apply the threshold independently to readable/writable sides where applicable; objectMode counts objects, byte mode counts bytes, and encoded readable strings use UTF-16 code units.

semantics.writable: write returns false at/above threshold after admitting chunk
semantics.readable: producer should stop pushing when threshold reached

caveats: Node defaults can change across Node versions; preserve explicit options and avoid baking a stale default into translation rules.
Continued writes after false are allowed but can buffer unboundedly and must not be silently dropped.

tests.name: object mode counts objects
tests.input: const {Writable}=require('node:stream'); let cb; const w=new Writable({objectMode:true,highWaterMark:1,write(v,e,d){cb=d}}); console.log(w.write({x:1})); cb();
tests.expected_behavior: prints false after one queued object reaches threshold 1

tests.name: threshold is not rejection
tests.input: const {Writable}=require('node:stream'); let callbacks=[]; const w=new Writable({highWaterMark:1,write(c,e,cb){callbacks.push(cb)}}); const a=w.write('a'); const b=w.write('b'); console.log(a,b,w.writableLength>=2); callbacks.shift()();
tests.expected_behavior: writes are admitted/buffered even when false signals backpressure
